title: A dry-run create allocated a port, wrote a record, and waited two minutes for nothing
foundBy: session agent, walking README.md and INSTALL.md as a first-time reader

evidence.verified: Before: `cs-sandbox --dry-run create drytest` left drytest in `cs-sandbox ls` holding port 2301 and 10.89.4.201, and `cs-sandbox start drytest` had to be killed at 60s. After: the same command prints the plan, reports `would create drydemo2`, exits 0 in seconds, and leaves neither a record nor an instance directory. TestSaveSkipsUnderDryRun and TestWaitReadyReturnsAtOnceUnderDryRun cover both halves, the second with a negative case that still fails a sandbox that never answers.

details:
MANUAL.md offers `--dry-run` as "print the external commands instead of running them", and its notes for agents say to use it to show a user the plan before acting.

`cs-sandbox --dry-run create <name>` did more than print. It allocated an IP and a host port, persisted the instance record, and wrote the per-instance seed (which carries an inherited agent login). Then it polled for a microVM that a dry run never booted, until the 120-second readiness budget ran out and the command failed with exit 1.

Interrupt it before that and the record survives: the name appears in `ls` as "stopped", holding a port and an address, with no sandbox behind it. `cs-sandbox start` on that record then waits the same two minutes.

Only `run.Exec` honoured the flag, so anything the CLI wrote itself was written for real.
